findings.title: DMARC not enforced (p=none): domain can be spoofed for BEC/wire fraud
findings.deal_impact: Domain can be spoofed for BEC/wire fraud, increasing fraud and phishing risk for fleet customers and finance processes; remediation is low-cost but should be verified pre-close.

remediation.summary: Move DMARC from p=none to quarantine then reject after monitoring rua reports and aligning SPF/DKIM.

findings.title: SPF uses soft/neutral fail
findings.deal_impact: Softfail weakens email authentication and spoofing resistance, compounding DMARC non-enforcement for a 201-1000 employee target.

remediation.summary: Inventory authorized senders and change SPF qualifier to -all once legitimate sources are confirmed.

findings.title: DNSSEC not enabled
findings.deal_impact: Lack of DNSSEC leaves DNS responses less protected against spoofing; low direct deal risk but indicates basic hygiene gaps.

remediation.summary: Enable DNSSEC at registrar/DNS provider and validate DS publication and resolver checks.

findings.title: Publicly logged hostnames suggest exposed admin/legacy/staging systems
findings.deal_impact: Publicly logged VPN, legacy, staging and old Jenkins names suggest attack surface that needs ownership/patch diligence; may affect cyber-insurance and Day-1 hardening scope.

remediation.summary: Validate ownership and exposure of risky hostnames, decommission legacy/staging systems or place behind authenticated access.

findings.title: Large certificate footprint relative to company size
findings.deal_impact: 47 hostnames for a 201-1000 employee company suggests sprawl and potential shadow assets, increasing inventory effort in value-creation planning.

remediation.summary: Reconcile CT hostnames to CMDB/asset inventory and remove or formally accept orphaned certificates/hosts.

findings.title: Deprecated TLS versions offered

evidence.excerpt: tls_support: TLSv1.0: true, TLSv1.1: true, TLSv1.2: true; tls_versions: [TLSv1.0, TLSv1.1, TLSv1.2]

findings.deal_impact: Deprecated TLS on www increases downgrade/crypto risk and may fail customer or insurer security questionnaires.

remediation.summary: Disable TLS 1.0/1.1 on www host, enforce TLS 1.2+ with modern ciphers and retest.

findings.title: HSTS not set
findings.deal_impact: Missing HSTS allows downgrade to HTTP on first visit; low standalone risk but an easy hygiene win for insurability.

remediation.summary: Set Strict-Transport-Security header with appropriate max-age on apex and www after confirming HTTPS coverage.

findings.title: Internet-facing appliance listed in CISA KEV (version not verified)

evidence.excerpt: CVE-PLACEHOLDER-0001, ExampleGate SSL-VPN 7.0.11, match_tier: appliance_exposed, match_level: product, note: KEV lists products, not affected versions; version not verified.

findings.deal_impact: Potential exposure: an internet-facing appliance fingerprint matches CISA KEV at product level only; urgent patch verification is needed as this could affect deal risk, insurance and closing conditions.

remediation.summary: Immediately verify ExampleGate SSL-VPN version/patch against KEV CVE, patch or isolate appliance, and review logs for exploitation.

findings.title: Publicly disclosed security incident in the last 24 months

evidence.excerpt: State AG breach notice 2025-08-14: unauthorized access to a customer support system; approx. 3,100 individuals notified. Entity match exact; disclosed_within_months: 14

findings.deal_impact: Recent disclosed breach (14 months ago, ~3,100 notified) raises regulatory, customer-trust and remediation diligence questions and may impact representations, insurance and escrow considerations.

remediation.summary: Diligence root cause, regulatory closure, notification costs and corrective actions from the 2025 incident; confirm no open obligations.

findings.title: SOC 2 exception in logical access controls (CC6.1)

evidence.excerpt: Exception noted. 4 of 25 sampled admin accounts were not enforced for MFA. These were service-desk accounts created via a legacy provisioning script that bypassed the conditional access policy.

findings.deal_impact: Four sampled administrative accounts bypassed MFA enforcement via a legacy provisioning process, indicating persistent privileged-access exposure until the migration of service-desk accounts is completed.

remediation.summary: Remediate CC6.1 exception: Exception noted. 4 of 25 sampled admin accounts were not enforced for MFA. These were service-desk accounts created via a legacy provisioning script that bypassed the conditional access policy.

findings.title: SOC 2 exception in logical access controls (CC6.2)

evidence.excerpt: Exception noted. 3 of 15 terminated users retained active access for 6, 11, and 19 business days respectively.

findings.deal_impact: Terminated users retained access for up to 19 business days, creating unauthorized-access risk and indicating manual de-provisioning did not meet the stated one-business-day requirement.

remediation.summary: Remediate CC6.2 exception: Exception noted. 3 of 15 terminated users retained active access for 6, 11, and 19 business days respectively.

findings.title: SOC 2 exception in security monitoring (CC7.2)

evidence.excerpt: Exception noted. For 2 consecutive weeks (Nov 10–23, 2025), alerts were forwarded to a decommissioned distribution list and were not reviewed.

findings.deal_impact: Two consecutive weeks without SIEM alert review created a monitoring blind spot during which security incidents could have gone undetected or been addressed late.

remediation.summary: Remediate CC7.2 exception: Exception noted. For 2 consecutive weeks (Nov 10–23, 2025), alerts were forwarded to a decommissioned distribution list and were not reviewed.

findings.title: SOC 2 exception in change management (CC8.1)

evidence.excerpt: Exception noted. 2 of 40 changes lacked documented approval (emergency hotfixes).

findings.deal_impact: Two emergency changes were deployed without documented peer approval, weakening change-control assurance, although management subsequently introduced post-deployment approval for emergency changes.

remediation.summary: Remediate CC8.1 exception: Exception noted. 2 of 40 changes lacked documented approval (emergency hotfixes).

findings.title: SOC 2 report period ended more than 90 days ago; no bridge letter provided
findings.deal_impact: Report period ended 2026-03-31, 213 days before the assessment date; controls may have changed since.

remediation.summary: Obtain a bridge letter covering through 2026-10-30.

findings.title: Critical subservice organization carved out of SOC 2 scope

evidence.locator: Section 1 — Independent Service Auditor's Report, Subservice organizations and Section 3.2 Infrastructure
evidence.excerpt: Nimbus Cloud Services is carved out of scope: infrastructure hosting.

findings.deal_impact: Nimbus Cloud Services (infrastructure hosting) is carved out of scope and is critical to production or in-scope data.

remediation.summary: Obtain the Nimbus Cloud Services SOC report and assess carve-out risk.

claim.speaker: Dana Reyes (CTO)
claim.text: Every admin account is behind MFA. No exceptions. That's been true for years. It's enforced through our conditional access policy.

contradictions.explanation: SOC 2 CC6.1 exception: 4 of 25 sampled admin accounts were not enforced for MFA, bypassing conditional access via a legacy provisioning script. This directly contradicts 'every admin account, no exceptions.'

claim.speaker: Dana Reyes (CTO)
claim.text: Offboarding is automated. HR flags the termination and access is revoked same day through our identity provider.

contradictions.explanation: SOC 2 CC6.2 exception: 3 of 15 terminated users retained active access for 6, 11, and 19 business days, contradicting automated same-day revocation on termination.

claim.speaker: Dana Reyes (CTO)
claim.text: We have a 24 7 SOC through our MSSP, every alert gets looked at, nothing sits.

contradictions.explanation: SOC 2 CC7.2 exception: for 2 consecutive weeks (Nov 10-23, 2025) alerts were forwarded to a decommissioned distribution list and were not reviewed, contradicting that every alert is looked at.

claim.speaker: Dana Reyes (CTO)
claim.text: We're fully locked down there. DMARC is enforced. Nobody can spoof our domain.

contradictions.explanation: DMARC record is v=DMARC1; p=none with policy none, so DMARC is not enforced and the domain can be spoofed, contradicting the claim of enforcement.

claim.speaker: Dana Reyes (CTO)
claim.text: No, nothing material. We've never had a breach.

contradictions.explanation: State AG breach notice 2025-08-14 reports unauthorized access to a customer support system with approx. 3,100 individuals notified, contradicting 'never had a breach.'

claim.speaker: Dana Reyes (CTO)
claim.text: We decommissioned the legacy stuff a while back. Everything external goes through the main app and the VPN.

contradictions.explanation: CT log presence alone doesn't prove a host is live; however, legacy-portal (last_seen 2026-07-22) and jenkins-old (last_seen 2026-08-14) have certificates within the last 12 months, showing active maintenance and contradicting decommissioning.

claim.speaker: Dana Reyes (CTO)
claim.text: Annual third party test. The last one came back clean. No highs.

contradictions.explanation: CC4.1-01 notes no exceptions, but states 2 high-severity findings were reported in the test, contradicting 'last one came back clean, no highs.'

claim.speaker: Dana Reyes (CTO)
claim.text: Daily backups to immutable storage in a second region and we do a restore test every quarter.

contradictions.explanation: SOC 2 A1.2-01 was control tested with no exceptions noted, which is positive evidence supporting the claimed backup and restore-testing control.

claim.speaker: Dana Reyes (CTO)
claim.text: We can get one. one we haven't needed it so far.

contradictions.explanation: No bridge letter was provided after the report period ended 2026-03-31, but management states it plans to obtain a bridge letter covering April 1, 2026 forward upon request, corroborating that one can be obtained.
